messages:
tim: thinking out loud — we need an automatic variant fallback when the primary model is saturated. goal: keep p99 latency SLOs without user-visible errors. thinking capacity-based failover + tier/region preferences. thoughts?

sara: +1. couple constraints: enterprise customers may have pinned variants for compliance, so opt-in override per-customer is required. also want telemetry hooks for every fallback event.

leila: agree on telemetry. propose an event: `fallback.triggered` with tags: customer_id, tier, primary_model, fallback_model, region, reason=(capacity|latency|error). that lets us build per-tenant dashboards.

mark: architecture question — where does the decision live? gateway layer (fast, simple) or scheduler/orchestrator (aware of queue depth, per-GPU metrics)? my vote: hybrid. gateway does quick checks + routing policy evaluation, orchestrator handles deeper capacity signals and can pre-warm alternatives.

tim: hybrid makes sense. gateway should have a lightweight policy engine so we can fail fast on known saturation signals and avoid adding RTT. orchestrator should stream richer signals (GPU util, queued-requests, batch sizes) to gateway via small-control plane.

leila: UX: console needs a new panel under Rollouts -> Fallback Rules. customers can set: allowed fallback variants (list), max-fallback-rate, prefer-regional-fallbacks, and a safety flag for pinned customers. also a preview that simulates traffic and shows expected fallback rate.

mark: important: don't surprise customers. add response header `x-redwood-fallback-used: true` and `x-redwood-primary-saturated: true` on fallback responses. also emit a one-line log with correlation id.

eva: policy semantics question — should fallback be deterministic ordering or weighted? e.g. enterprise => prefer 13b in eu then 7b-quant, but for lower tiers we might want weighted round-robin to balance cost. We need both.

tim: implement both. policy model: `primary`, `fallbacks: [{model:..., weight:..., region_pref:...}]`, `scope: {customer_tier, region}`, `max_rate`. gateway samples according to weights but honors max_rate.

leila: on quotas: if a customer is hitting their quota, do not auto-fallback to cheaper variant unless they have allowed it. fallback should never bypass billing/quota checks. also record billing_model in the event.

mark: infra-bot: can you show current signals we expose for capacity?

infra-bot: available signals: `gpu_util` (per-pool), `queue_depth` (per-deployment), `avg_batch_size`, `kv_cache_hit_rate`. we can stream these over pubsub to gateway every 500ms.

eva: nice. for saturation detection heuristic: `saturated = queue_depth > 0.8*pool_size OR gpu_util > 0.92 for 10s OR avg_latency increase > 30%`. open to tuning.

tim: agree. also add cooldown windows per-customer to avoid flip-flopping: once fallback used for a request, lock routing for that customer for 30s unless explicit override.

leila: monitoring needs: per-customer fallback-rate, fallback-latency-delta, quality-regressions (we can feed evals). create a dashboard tile in Console: Fallbacks by Tier / Region. alert on >1% fallback rate for enterprise tier.

mark: internal API debate — allow per-request header `X-Fallback-Policy: prefer-cost`? pros: apps can tune. cons: it's an attack vector to force lower-cost models and hurt quality. lean to exposing at tenant + route level, not per-request, unless route is internal-trusted.

tim: let's scope: API supports tenant-level and route-level policies. add feature flag to enable per-request overrides for internal service accounts only. documented in API docs and gated by role.

eva: about rollout UX — we should surface rollback recommendations when fallback QPS > threshold and quality delta > threshold. tie to Rollouts so product can quick revert.

leila: also add a simulator endpoint in Console where SEs can upload a small trace and see what routing decisions would have been with a given policy. helps debug surprises.

mark: ops runbook notes: when large-scale primary saturation happens, auto-fallback should be conservative: prefer regional same-variant first (if cross-region is disallowed), then smaller quantized variants, then open-source compatible models. escalate if fallback rate grows > 10% global.

tim: security/compliance: private deployments should default to fallback disabled unless customer explicitly enables it. log consent.

sara: nice list. next steps: 1) design gateway policy proto 2) add telemetry event spec 3) console mockups for fallback rules + simulator 4) strand for per-tenant opt-in. volunteers?

leila: I'll take telemetry spec + dashboard mocks.

mark: I can own gateway proto + orchestrator control-plane hooks.

tim: I'll prototype console UI + simulator.

eva: I'll write the saturation heuristics test harness and help tune thresholds.

sara: thanks — create RFC in Google Drive and link it here when ready. add a short section on expected SLO changes and customer communication template.

tim: drafted initial doc: https://drive.redwood.company/drive/fallback-rfc — putting notes in it now.

mark: putting a small PR up to expose `fallback.triggered` in telemetry schema repo.

infra-bot: created task INF-4821: stream capacity signals to gateway, assigned to mark.

sara: perfect. let's sync on Monday 10am to review the mockups and telemetry schema. :thumbsup:
